---
title: "El Niño / PDO"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
```

Two Pacific climate indices:

- `nino34_anom`: monthly Niño 3.4 SST anomaly, unsmoothed, NOAA CPC (1950–present). Source: <https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/data/indices/> (`ersst5.nino.mth.91-20.ascii`)
- `pdo`: monthly Pacific Decadal Oscillation index, NOAA NCEI (1854–present, joined to the overlapping range). Source: <https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/monitoring/pdo/>

Both are monthly and unsmoothed — unlike ONI's 3-month rolling mean, which would introduce autocorrelation by construction and violate `model-assumptions.qmd`. The ENSO–PDO correlation is known to be non-stationary across decadal climate regimes (e.g. the 1976–77 Pacific climate shift), making this a natural real-data test case for ECE.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: elnino-load

nino <- read_table(
  "../data/real-data/elnino/nino34-raw.txt",
  skip = 1,
  col_names = c("year", "month", "nino12", "nino12_anom", "nino3", "nino3_anom",
                "nino4", "nino4_anom", "nino34", "nino34_anom")
) |>
  select(year, month, nino34_anom)

pdo <- read_table(
  "../data/real-data/elnino/pdo-raw.txt",
  skip = 2,
  col_names = c("year", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun",
                "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec")
) |>
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "month_name", values_to = "pdo") |>
  mutate(month = match(month_name, month.abb)) |>
  select(year, month, pdo)

X <- inner_join(nino, pdo, by = c("year", "month")) |>
  arrange(year, month) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", year, month))) |>
  filter(pdo > -99)
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-elnino-raw
#| fig-cap: "Niño 3.4 anomaly and PDO index, monthly."

X |>
  select(date, nino34_anom, pdo) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, value, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Niño 3.4 Anomaly vs. PDO Index", x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: elnino-matrix

X_mat <- as.matrix(X[, c("nino34_anom", "pdo")])
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-elnino}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_mat[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Month index (1950–present)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R acf-elnino-naive}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  acf(X_mat[, i], main = "", xlab = "", ylab = colnames(X_mat)[i])
}
mtext("Lag (months)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R acf-elnino-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_sip_acf(X_mat)
```

:::

## Trend

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R trend-elnino-naive}
#| echo: false

win <- 25 # matches the window used in mental-load.qmd
plot_naive_terms(X_mat, window = win)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R trend-elnino-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_ece_terms(X_mat, window = win)
```

:::

:::

Naive ACF (base-R `acf()`): lag-1 autocorrelation ~0.9–0.95 for both series, decaying slowly — violates `model-assumptions.qmd`. Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF (`SIP::SIP.acf`): both series read as uncorrelated at every lag. `SIP.acf` discounts mean-shift-induced autocorrelation, so the gap suggests the naive values are inflated by the regime-shifting mean, not pure error autocorrelation — though this doesn't prove the residual process is white.

Faded bars in the Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF mark lags where `SIP.acf`'s own difference-based variance estimate came out negative and fell back to the naive `var(x)` (see `plot_sip_acf()`/`sip_acf_with_fallback()` in `R/plot-helpers.R`). Since `var(x)` is inflated by mean shifts relative to the variance `SIP.acf` is meant to use, those lags' values rest on a mismatched denominator and are less trustworthy than the rest. For `nino34_anom` every lag shown falls back (fully faded); for `pdo` none do.

Naive Trend (`plot_naive_terms`) removes a rolling mean per series, then plots the raw product of those residuals (gray) with its own rolling mean on top (blue) against the global mean (dashed) — same grammar as the Mean-Shift-Invariant Trend (`plot_ece_terms`), but mean-removal is a rolling mean instead of ECE's difference-based construction. `plot_ece_terms` is what ECE's test statistic actually uses, and it still drifts from its global mean over multi-year stretches — some non-stationarity survives mean-shift removal either way.

## Downsampling

Keep every 3rd observation (`k = 3`), matching `mental-load.qmd` and ENSO/PDO's typical 3-month tracking cadence.

```{R downsample-elnino}
#| echo: false

k_ds <- 3
idx  <- seq(1, nrow(X_mat), by = k_ds)
X_ds <- X_mat[idx, ]
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-elnino-downsampled}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  plot(X_ds[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X_ds)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Index (every 3rd month)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R acf-elnino-downsampled-naive}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(2, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:2) {
  acf(X_ds[, i], main = "", xlab = "", ylab = colnames(X_ds)[i])
}
mtext("Lag (every 3rd month)", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R acf-elnino-downsampled-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_sip_acf(X_ds)
```

:::

## Trend

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Naive

```{R trend-elnino-downsampled-naive}
#| echo: false

win_ds <- 25 # same fixed window as the full-sample case
plot_naive_terms(X_ds, window = win_ds)
```

### Mean-Shift-Invariant

```{R trend-elnino-downsampled-invariant}
#| echo: false

plot_ece_terms(X_ds, window = win_ds)
```

:::

:::

Mean-Shift-Invariant ACF stays near-zero before and after downsampling. Naive ACF drops but doesn't clear: lag-1 autocorrelation ~0.95→0.76 (`nino34_anom`), ~0.98→0.70 (`pdo`). `k = 3` is not enough to whiten either series — ENSO/PDO persistence runs months to years, unlike the sensor-artifact case in `mental-load.qmd`. A larger stride or explicit pre-whitening would be needed to satisfy the naive no-autocorrelation assumption; the mean-shift-invariant view suggests less of that persistence reaches the quantity ECE actually uses.
